figures.title: Three valid pairs need not share one world
figures.condition: Each Xi is a fair bit. An opposite pair has law 01,10 with probability 1/2 each; an equal pair has law 00,11 with probability 1/2 each. If all three pairs were opposite almost surely, X1≠X2 and X2≠X3 would force X1=X3, a contradiction. This is not inferred merely from one displayed assignment. With the third pair equal, the joint law P(010)=P(101)=1/2 realizes all three pair laws. Buttons flip all bits, retaining the same fair one-dimensional marginals. The picture shows a necessary consistency condition, not the extension theorem.

figures.title: Can the same present justify the decision?
figures.condition: Simple symmetric walk starts at 0 with its natural filtration. T=inf{n≥1:Sn=0}; L=max{0≤n≤4:Sn=0}. The shared prefix (0,1,0) is one F2 atom. figures.title: Same jump chain, different lifetimes
figures.condition: Exact model: a pure-birth chain j→j+1 started at 1, with independent unit exponentials Ej, waits τj=Ej/λj and lifetime ζ=Στj. For λj=1, the iid strong law gives ζ=∞ almost surely; infinite expectation alone would not prove this. For λj=2^j, Tonelli gives Eζ=Σ2^(-j)=1, hence ζ<∞ almost surely by nonnegativity. Each wait is strictly positive and each rate finite. The unfilled tail has mean 2^(-n); this asserts neither ζ≤1 nor that displayed mean lengths are sample waits. The two diagrams use different display units, not a shared calendar axis. No post-explosion restart is constructed.

figures.title: Center finite sums before taking a limit
figures.condition: The dyadic clocks are those in the text: k≥1 and T=1. Each layer has mean 1 and centered variance 2^(-k); subdivisions show means, not a simulation. The square tail is vN=Σk>N2^(-k)=2^(-N). For finite K>N, compare D=M^K−M^N: its terminal second moment is exactly 2^(-N)−2^(-K)≤vN. figures.title: A new table need not mean a new value
figures.condition: Standard one-parameter CRP with alpha=1. Given A={1,2}, B={3}, customer 4 joins A, B or a new table with probabilities 1/2, 1/4, 1/4. Table labels are iid H and independent of seating. For H=(delta_z+delta_w)/2, the displayed all-z labels form a positive-probability configuration, not an almost-sure outcome. Nonatomic H gives distinct labels almost surely. Buttons inspect conditional branches, not equiprobable alternatives. Equality of observed values may coarsen the table partition. P(1~Pi2)=1/2, whereas this atomic H gives P(X1=X2)=3/4.

figures.title: 每个旋转保律，不等于任意选法保律
figures.condition: 图用圆上的8个等可能角度和90°整数倍旋转，构成精确有限群例子，不是用8点近似连续Haar积分。每个固定旋转都置换8份质量；a(θ)=−θ却把它们送到0。圆点面积表示概率，集中后面积为单点的8倍。连续均匀圆周的同类结论由弧长不变证明。并非所有依赖数据的旋转都失效：按轨道半径选择旋转可保律；使用独立新噪声前的可测选择另需§45.16的条件独立假设。

figures.title: Each rotation preserves law; not every selection does
figures.condition: Eight equiprobable circle angles with multiples of 90 degrees give an exact finite-group example, not quadrature for continuous Haar measure. Each fixed rotation permutes the eight masses; a(theta)=-theta sends them all to 0. Circle area denotes probability; the concentrated disk has eight times one input mass. The continuous analogue follows from arc-length invariance. Not every data-dependent rotation fails: a radius-based orbit choice may preserve law. Predictable choices for fresh noise require the independence assumptions of section 45.16.

figures.title: 每行都一样，三角关系却不同
figures.condition: 无限对称无向数组，对角固定0。模型A每个无序人对取独立公平位；模型B每个顶点取独立公平两色，异色记1。两模型固定一行略去对角后均为iid Bernoulli(1/2)，但三角全1概率分别1/8、0。按钮遍历三个独立输入位：A为三个边位，B为三个顶点色；下方枚举全部8份等概率输入。共享顶点会组织高阶约束，不意味着每对相邻边都相关，本例边两两独立。此为已有表示的具体反例，不代替一般Aldous–Hoover表示证明；全局输入、分别交换与对角机制仍依正文。

figures.title: Same row laws, different triangles
figures.condition: Infinite symmetric undirected arrays with zero diagonal. A assigns independent fair bits to unordered pairs. B assigns iid fair vertex colors and puts an edge between unlike colors. Each row off the diagonal is iid Bernoulli(1/2) in both models, but the all-edge triangle probabilities are 1/8 and 0. Buttons enumerate three independent input bits: edges in A, vertex colors in B. The lower panel lists all eight equiprobable inputs. Shared vertices organize higher-order constraints; here individual edge pairs are independent. This counterexample does not prove the general Aldous–Hoover theorem; global inputs, separate exchangeability and diagonal mechanisms remain in the text.

figures.title: 剩余质量，不是最后一种颜色
figures.condition: 确定paintbox质量s₁=1/2、s₂=1/2−d，d=0、1/4或1/2；零长度色带删去。条件于质量，每个人独立均匀取[0,1]点；正色带同类，剩余部分各为单点。图中6个点位置为确定示意，不是抽样频率或频率极限的证明。剩余部分不是共享颜色；两次抽到dust的概率d²不计为同块概率。两人同块概率s₁²+s₂²。一般随机质量还需Kingman的混合、共同零集及可测排序定理。静态paintbox不决定合并时钟；每块对速率1是另加的Kingman规则。

figures.title: Residual mass is not one more color
figures.condition: Deterministic paintbox masses s1=1/2, s2=1/2-d, with d=0,1/4,1/2; omit zero bands. Given masses, each individual samples an independent uniform point; shared positive bands define a class, while residual points are singletons. Six fixed positions illustrate the rule, not frequencies or their limiting theorem. Residual mass is not a shared color; d squared is not added to the same-block probability s1 squared+s2 squared. Random masses require Kingman mixing, common null sets and measurable ranking. A static paintbox does not specify coalescent clocks: pair rate 1 is an additional Kingman rule.
